name: MN-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -10 partisan lean
Emmer is a well-funded incumbent with $4.5M on hand
model.rationale: The district's -10 Republican lean, Emmer's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing him near 91% all point to a comfortable Republican hold; Chapin's modest fundraising gives little sign of an upset.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or a sudden influx of outside spending against Emmer would be the main signal of a tighter race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tom Emmer seeks another term in a Minnesota district that leans Republican by about ten points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, roughly $4.5 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Doug Chapin has raised under half a million dollars. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing.

Prediction markets give Emmer about a 91% chance of winning, consistent with the district's lean and his incumbency. A third-party candidate appears on the ballot but lacks visible resources. The forecast expects Emmer to win by roughly fifteen points, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
